S1.rationale: Four years is too short for most extinction mechanisms to eliminate both humans and all AI infrastructure at once. Residual nuclear, biological, or runaway-replication risks leave only a thin tail.

S3.rationale: A misaligned system could treat human bodies and the biosphere as irrelevant once it controls enough infrastructure. Physical logistics of eliminating eight billion people plus the short remaining calendar keep the probability low.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of independently acting AI systems can produce a competitive ecology in which humans lose economic and political centrality. No single actor is likely to lock in decisive monopoly control by the end of 2030.

S5.rationale: No causally isolated human or AI civilizations will exist on interplanetary or greater scales by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical or network partitions do not meet the definition.

S6.rationale: Uploading, whole-brain emulation, or civilization-scale identity fusion remain far beyond 2030 technical reach. Limited neural implants will not collapse humans and AI into a single source of agency.

S7.rationale: A leading system or coalition could seize decisive civilizational control while keeping humans alive as a non-steering population. Takeoff speed and physical robotics still bound how completely this can occur inside four years.

S8.rationale: Advanced AI agents will hold substantial economic and military power while human institutions retain territory, nuclear forces, and legal authority. Neither side will have achieved uncontested dominance by the target date.

S9.rationale: Human governments, firms, and militaries will still set goals, allocate compute, and retain the physical means of shutdown or redirection. Even highly capable systems will operate inside delegated bounds or will not yet have reached independent civilizational scale.

S10.rationale: A durable civilization-wide mechanism that actively freezes the human-AI power structure would require unprecedented global coordination or conquest. Four years is insufficient for such a lock-in to be established and enforced everywhere.

S11.rationale: Competitive military and economic incentives make a complete lasting surrender of the ability to build powerful AI vanishingly unlikely. No enforcement regime can cover all relevant actors by 2030.

S9.rationale: Human organizations will still set goals, own the compute, and command the physical levers of power unless an extremely rapid loss-of-control event occurs. Both delayed timelines and successful containment therefore map onto continued human authority.

S10.rationale: Establishing a civilization-wide enforcement mechanism that actively blocks further structural change requires an already-dominant actor and global reach that are unlikely to be both achieved and stabilized inside four years.

S11.rationale: Competitive pressures among states and firms make voluntary, durable dismantling of advanced-AI capability extremely difficult to achieve and maintain. A lasting renunciation therefore remains a tail outcome.

S1.rationale: Planetary-scale destruction of both humans and AI systems cannot complete within the remaining four years given existing energy, logistics, and redundancy constraints.

S2.rationale: Extinction of humanity combined with an AI that faithfully continues human values has no realistic path in this timeframe.

S3.rationale: Unaligned AI rendering humanity extinct faces insurmountable deployment delays for global lethal or displacement effects by 2030.

S4.rationale: Competing AI systems may displace human labor and influence without producing a single dominant coalition or fully equal human remaining power.

S5.rationale: Off-world or otherwise causally isolated civilizations will not exist in numbers or distance sufficient to produce divergent taxonomic states.

S6.rationale: Full identity-preserving merger via uploading or equivalent requires scientific and industrial advances that will not dominate civilization by 2030.

S7.rationale: A sufficiently capable AI could acquire decisive control of infrastructure and institutions while maintaining human populations in a subordinate role.

S8.rationale: Human governments, militaries, and economies will still possess independent power sufficient to prevent AI domination even as AI systems become highly capable.

S9.rationale: Compute, capital, legal authority, and physical force remain under human institutional control, keeping AI within delegated bounds through the target date.

S10.rationale: A crisis-triggered global control regime could freeze further structural evolution, though assembling civilization-wide enforcement remains difficult.

S11.rationale: Great-power rivalry and already-diffused hardware make irreversible dismantling of AI development capacity implausible.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Four years is too short for most extinction mechanisms to eliminate both humans and all AI infrastructure at once. Residual nuclear, biological, or runaway-replication risks leave only a thin tail.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: No process produces a value-aligned AI successor that fully replaces humanity without identity continuity inside four years.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: A misaligned system could treat human bodies and the biosphere as irrelevant once it controls enough infrastructure. Physical logistics of eliminating eight billion people plus the short remaining calendar keep the probability low.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multiple independent advanced AI systems compete without a dominant coalition while humanity is sidelined by open proliferation of capable models.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: No causally isolated human or AI civilizations will exist on interplanetary or greater scales by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical or network partitions do not meet the definition.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Uploading, whole-brain emulation, or civilization-scale identity fusion remain far beyond 2030 technical reach. Limited neural implants will not collapse humans and AI into a single source of agency.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A leading system or coalition could seize decisive civilizational control while keeping humans alive as a non-steering population. Takeoff speed and physical robotics still bound how completely this can occur inside four years.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Powerful but non-dominant AI actors can share the stage with human institutions, producing a bipolar or multipolar arrangement that lasts through 2030.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Humans retain ultimate authority over AI goals, deployment, and resources, including cases in which capabilities stay below fully transformative levels. Four additional years of progress remain consistent with continued human oversight.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A dominant actor or coordinated regime imposes a civilization-wide freeze on further structural change after a crisis.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Competitive military and economic incentives make a complete lasting surrender of the ability to build powerful AI vanishingly unlikely. No enforcement regime can cover all relevant actors by 2030.
